chapter_title: The Catechumen asks the Apostle: will Rest come about for Someone who has come out of the Body, if the Saints pray over and make an Alms-offering for him?
chapter_note: The chapter opens and closes in dialogue-frame and quickly pivots into two substantial archetypal “entreaty” narratives (Mother of Life → Living Spirit; then the Five → Third Ambassador) that are strongly cosmological and systematic (CORE). After these, the text drifts into church practice around alms/remembrance for the dead with heavy institutional vocabulary and a seam-flagged ecclesial extension (PASTORAL), consistent with the strong editorial-fatigue signal. A few late sections retain small embedded cosmological phrases (MIXED).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic scene-setting (“Once again… our enlightener… congregation”) is hagiographic frame.
Direct address + beseeching formula (“I beseech you, my master”) is dialogue frame.
Problem framed in terms of saints’ intercession and retribution-for-deeds; this is community practice/theodicy rather than impersonal cosmological mechanism.
Second beseeching formula and appeal to what is ‘honoured amongst people’—editorial framing.
Institutional categories (elect), faith-language, and direct pastoral assurance; also begins with dialogue attribution (“Then the apostle…”).

paragraphs.core_text: For this entreaty has been since the beginning [...] the gods first made entreaty of their Father. They were granted their entreaty and their request.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed ecclesial/Christian graft: reference to “the holy church that assumes the flesh” and invocation of “the son, the Christ,” which shifts from cosmic prototype to institutional/Christian application.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with cosmic-historical claim (gods’ primordial entreaty) typical of archetypal substrate, then pivots outward to church/Christ (late application/overlay).
Programmatic transition (“I will instruct you… in what form…”) functions as discourse scaffolding, not cosmological mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.272⟩ The Great Spirit, the Mother of Life, she claimed and prayed and besought and glorified and praised the first established one, who is the Father. She besought him an entreaty. She claimed of him a request. She received a great gift; she and the many powers with her.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Archetypal cosmic beings (Mother of Life, Father) in impersonal prototype narrative; wholly within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: She besought an entreaty on behalf of the First Man, because of how he had come forth and thrown himself down. He became distant from the Mother of Life. He separated from her and gave himself; in great affliction. He joined war on earth with the destruction and the grief and the weakness; in the worlds of Darkness; in the abysses made of fear; in the midst of the demons' ditch; amongst the powers of the Devil!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic Manichaean cosmological drama (First Man in Darkness/abyss) narrated as prototype; no institutional reach.

paragraphs.core_text: Indeed, he is like a king standing in the midst of his enemies. And when the Mother of Life petitioned and prayed and glorified and praised the Father, the first established one, she did petition him that he might send a power; a protector and redeemer and helper for the son of God who is set in affliction.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still cosmic prototype (rescue-helper request). “son of God” here functions as a cosmic category within the First Man episode, not a Gospel citation.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.273⟩ Now, just as she had besought and interceded, so likewise was her prayer fulfilled and received into the presence of the Father of Greatness. He turned and gave to her her entreaty: the great power, the Living Spirit, the giver of ease. The Mother of Life and the Living Spirit came with great power to the borders of the territory. They brought the First Man up from that war and struggle, wherein he is set.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal soteriology: Father of Greatness → Living Spirit → extraction of First Man; impersonal cosmic mechanics despite a transitional ‘now/likewise’.

paragraphs.core_text: He gave himself as a grace for the Mother of Life. He became estranged and far from her, the one whom his enemies (place) in great affliction, the one who is in the land of Darkness since he became weak.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the prototype rescue situation; Darkness treated as cosmic domain.

paragraphs.core_text: The Living Spirit grasped and took him in. He freed him. He set him right and gave him ease in the land of rest [...] the Living Spirit, the first giver of ease [...] the will of these three. The welcomer [...] find with the welcomer that [...
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic rescue sequence + triadic ‘will of these three’ motif typical of older structural teaching; no church application.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] a great power [...] of the loved one [...] the First Man who had been far away. He had become distant. She had besought on his behalf. He was set fast in affliction. (The Living Spirit) went to the place of destruction and weakness, the one that freed and redeemed him and gave him ease from the affliction. He set him right with rest and joy. He has himself become rested, with him for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same archetypal entreaty/provision logic entirely within cosmic geography (place of destruction vs rest/joy).
Meta-instruction (“See now, I have taught you…”) functions as rhetorical recap in teacher-to-audience voice rather than substrate exposition.
Directly applies the archetype to saints praying over the dead; institutional category (‘faithful saints’) and pastoral reassurance.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] and they built the universe and completed it with its firmaments, with its wheels, with the ships of light that are in the heights, with its fastenings, with its earths and its walls, with its vessels. They completed the universe and set it right by the fathers of light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic construction catalogue (firmaments/wheels/ships of light) is system-internal and characteristic of the oldest cosmological layer.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.274⟩ Then, the Great Spirit stood with the Beloved of the Lights, the Great Builder with the Living Spirit and the First Man. These five stood to prayer; they glorified and praised the Father, the first established one. They besought of him an entreaty. They claimed of him a request, that he might give them the power [...] the leader, a guide to all the things of activity that they had constructed. That he might come and purify the living soul that is set in affliction.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Structured ‘five’ assembly of cosmic beings and an archetypal request for a salvific agent; fully internal to the cosmic hierarchy.

paragraphs.core_text: They prayed and besought their Father, and he received from them their prayer [...] he gave them their entreaty and their request [...] he summoned from him [...] which is the Third Ambassador. He, he came from the power of his greatness. He saw the entire soul, how it is entangled in a chain and set fast. It sees the things of activity that his brothers have constructed, that have come from the heights. Again, he saw the living soul, that it is entangled and set fast in a great torture. It is oppressed in the stink of the abyss that is joined with it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Archetypal granting of the Third Ambassador and description of the soul’s entanglement—cosmic mechanics rather than moral exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: And therefore, he, the Ambassador [...] in his charity. So, he revealed his way, before this underworld that is dug deep down, to free the living soul. He redeemed it from all the fleshes of death wherein it is pained. He gave it ease. He set it right in the place of rest and joy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Salvific descent/way-revelation in underworld terms; still cosmos→cosmos (underworld, fleshes of death, rest/joy).

paragraphs.core_text: And again, he too, the Ambassador, he fulfilled the will of these three; the will of his brothers who had besought the Father for him. They claimed of him a request, together with the [...] of the Father, the one that [...] he gave the entreaty that they had besought of him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Triadic ‘will of these three’ coordination + request/fulfilment motif; system-internal.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the transferral of the living soul that he had freed. He released it and gave it ease from the affliction. He became king and first to the entire body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Degree/office statement about the freed soul and kingship—cosmological hierarchy language.
Meta-recap (“Behold, I have instructed you…”)—teacherly stitching rather than substrate content.
Explicit institutional address (elect, catechumen) and application of the prototype to community prayer practice.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, let us come to the third entreaty when they besought him the third time [...] displayed his image [...] he hid his image from the [...] he stood firm [...] they revealed [...] the light [...] the First Man [...] mock [...] to him in [...] which is exalted [...] garment [...] they were freed [...] to him [...] their voice [...] the body [...] prayer [...] it [...] beseech [...] the body [...] beseech [...] she besought [...] in [...] be free [...] Ambassador [...] and also [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Despite heavy lacunae, the surviving nouns/actors (First Man, light, image/garment, Ambassador) remain within the cosmic drama rather than church practice.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.276⟩ [...] with the living ones and [...] for ever [...] the first [...] from the [...] he gave him the hope [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragmentary continuation with no institutional markers; likely part of the same cosmological sequence.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, Jesus the Splendour perfected the will [...] the will [...] they found the light [...] the will of the [...] that he had [...] he gave them the power that is Jesus the Splendour. He granted the will of the elements. [...] for ever. This first [...] he was humbled, he was made free [...] the [...]-ness is displayed to his enemies. He received the hope [...] reveal [...] Jesus the Splendour, the light power [...] and the entreaty of the [...] of light [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: “Jesus the Splendour” appears as a named cosmological power operating with ‘elements’ and ‘will’—not a Gospel citation; register is cosmic despite lacunae.
Second-person anchoring (“you are set firm… Happen you know…”) indicates application voice; too fragmentary to isolate a clean core block.
Mentions “petition of the holy church,” anchoring the mechanism in institutional practice.
Alms/remembrance for the dead and ‘four victories’—explicit community rite framing.

paragraphs.core_text: [...] of the living soul that is entangled and bound in the entire universe. For it shall be freed and cleansed and purified and redeemed
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the explicit application hook (“The first:” and “by cause of him”) that ties the cosmological liberation formula to a donor’s alms act.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Contains a compact, system-internal liberation formula embedded inside a late ritual list for alms-for-the-dead.
Institutional mapping to ‘holy church’ and ‘children of the church’; alms as ecclesial benefit.
Too fragmentary, but appears as part of the late ‘victories’ enumeration tied to intercession.
Extended kinship list (father/mother/son/daughter) + alms/remembrance ‘of the church’—practical community instruction.
Catechumen + alms and sins language in communal register; not cosmological exposition.
Fragmentary but dominated by kinship/catechumen/sin vocabulary; institutional context.
Fragmentary, but includes catechumen/intercession logic and a Christian token (“Cross”); overall an applied exhortative register.
Analogy about a bound sinner and a relative petitioning—moral/legal example, not cosmic architecture.
Fragment within the same legal-analogy section.
Speaker attribution + restatement of the catechumen’s question in didactic prose; editorial frame within the analogy.
Charity-as-payment logic inside the analogy; community ethics/application.
Seam-flagged institutional extension: catechumen/remembrance in church/holy church + saints’ sin-entreaty; cosmos→church application dominates the whole paragraph.
Although it uses ‘living soul’ vocabulary, the paragraph operates in intercessory/forgiveness-of-sins practice (“in the name of that person”), i.e., applied community soteriology.

paragraphs.core_text: It goes into the land of light [...] comes about for it; and it goes to the land of life and rest [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the reciprocal-application setup (“Just as ease has come about… by cause of this soul… by cause of this soul”) which ties the ascent motif to the intercession scenario.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Contains a clean cosmological ascent-to-Light clause embedded in a reciprocal-intercession argument.
Direct charge to catechumens to perform alms/remembrances; explicit transmigration count; dialogue attribution (“Then speaks the apostle…”) and strong institutional practice.
Formulaic closing response: praise/obeisance/gratitude to the master—hagiographic closure.
